experiment: 034 fixed input-cell-per-query queue policy CPU cost replay
frozen_policy: Ascending Fraction(sum all train input+output cells plus all test input cells,n_test_queries); ties ascending task_id
clock: Seconds since the earliest original025 task_start; shared Notebook setup/model loading before that origin is excluded
scheduling_model: Four nonpreemptive workers with fixed observed initial task offsets. Every task duration is its own closed observed task_end-task_start interval, reused as a deterministic service time on any worker. Assign next task to earliest available worker; tie rank. No per-query oracle or correctness is consulted.
query_event_model: For each rescheduled task shift only the timestamps of its observed search_start/search_end events by the task new start. A task/query search before cutoff is coverage only, not accuracy or necessarily completed scoring. Four observed completed search batches are a search-completeness diagnostic.
limitations: This is deterministic replay on already exposed025 public tasks, not a real033 GPU run or hidden240-task replication.
025 used original CPU NLL rather than033 GPU NLL; timings do not transfer exactly.
Task duration changes with rank, warmup/compilation, numerical path, device scheduling and earlier task history; these counterfactual effects are omitted.
The service-time model excludes gaps between tasks and all setup before the first task_start; actual stage events are not synthesized outside the measured tasks.
Existing per-task1200s soft truncation and all known query events are preserved in replay; four-batch coverage is not EM@2.
More completed tasks/queries in a replay cannot establish more correct hidden answers or an improved competition score.
No timing threshold or policy coefficient was selected by querying predictions or query labels.
